title: user.deleted
description: Emitted by the User Service when a user is soft-deleted (typical trigger: GDPR right-to-be-forgotten). Consumed by Notification Service (suppress further sends) and Recommendation Engine (purge per-user derived state). Topic: user.deleted. Partition key: user_id. Subject in Schema Registry: user.deleted-value. Satisfies AAP R-30 (topic name mirrors event name), R-31 (version field for backward-compatible evolution), R-32 (producer does not enumerate consumers), R-33 (event is self-contained — no callback to the producer required).

event_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this event instance. Used by consumers as the idempotency key when processing the message.

version.description: Event payload schema version per AAP R-31. Incremented when the schema evolves backward-compatibly. Consumers MUST tolerate values they do not yet know about.

user_id.description: User aggregate identifier whose lifecycle ended. Stable for the lifetime of the user. Equals the `id` column of `users.users` and the partition key of all `user.*` Kafka events.

external_auth_id.description: Stable identifier from the Auth Service `sub` (subject) claim. Carried so downstream services can correlate with auth-side state and propagate the deletion to systems that index on the external identifier.

deleted_at.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC, with offset suffix) at which the soft-delete was committed in the User Service. Mirrors the `users.deleted_at` column.

reason.description: Canonical reason code that drives downstream cleanup behavior. USER_REQUESTED: customer-initiated deletion. ADMIN_DELETED: removed via support tooling by an authorized operator. GDPR_RIGHT_TO_BE_FORGOTTEN: regulatory data-erasure request — downstream services MUST purge derived state. ACCOUNT_INACTIVE: long-dormant cleanup by a scheduled job. TERMS_VIOLATION: trust-and-safety enforcement action.

user_version.description: Optional. Optimistic-concurrency token (the `version` column of `users.users`) at the moment the deletion was committed. Allows consumers to discard stale `user.updated` events that arrive after this delete due to out-of-order delivery.
